title: Malicious SHA-256 file hash ef251d66663f… (OffSeq Mirage)
description: The OffSeq Mirage honeypot sensors detected a malicious file identified by the SHA-256 hash ef251d66663f4a97882fcdcf7622a377c2b3068c26763f73e1ec0a81136342dc. This file was observed 10 times on October 24, 2026, associated with attacker activity using the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer). The hash corresponds to a malicious payload that could be a dropper, web shell, miner, or post-exploitation tool. No specific software versions or products are affected, and no known exploits in the wild have been reported. The threat is an indicator of compromise (IOC) useful for detection and response efforts.

The activity involved the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1105, which is ingress tool transfer, indicating the file was staged or delivered as part of an attack. The file hash fingerprints a malicious payload that may function as a dropper, web shell, miner, or post-exploitation tool. This indicator can be used to match against files in environments and endpoint detection and response (EDR) or antivirus (AV) systems to identify potential compromise. There is no information on affected software versions or active exploitation in the wild.
aiImpact: The presence of this malicious file hash indicates potential attacker activity involving the transfer of a malicious payload into a target environment. The payload could enable further compromise through dropping additional malware, establishing remote access (web shell), mining cryptocurrency, or post-exploitation actions. However, no direct evidence of exploitation or impact severity is provided. The impact is primarily detection of attacker tool presence and potential for subsequent malicious actions.
